root_cause.text: The probe function in the STM32 USB PHY controller driver used a less-than-or-equal bound check (`index > usbphyc->nphys`) instead of a strict less-than check (`index >= usbphyc->nphys`), allowing an out-of-bounds array access when the device tree `reg` property specifies an index equal to the number of elements in the `usbphyc->phys[]` array.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states: "The 'index' variable is used as an index into the usbphyc->phys[] array which has usbphyc->nphys elements. So if it is equal to usbphyc->nphys then it is one element out of bounds." The patch changes the condition from `index > usbphyc->nphys` to `index >= usbphyc->nphys`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix off-by-one error in index validation to prevent accessing beyond the allocated phy array.
intent_record.what: Changed the index validation condition from 'index > usbphyc->nphys' to 'index >= usbphyc->nphys' in the stm32_usbphyc_probe function.
intent_record.how: This change treats an index equal to the number of phys (nphys) as invalid, preventing out-of-bounds access when indexing an array of size nphys.

grouping_result.intent: Fix off-by-one error in index validation to prevent accessing beyond the allocated phy array.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly fixes the off-by-one error in index validation that allowed out-of-bounds access, which is the exact vulnerability root cause.

candidates.rationale: The condition uses '>' instead of '>=', allowing an out-of-bounds access when index equals usbphyc->nphys, because array indices are 0-based and the allocated size is nphys.

vuln_statements.explanation: Uses '>' instead of '>=' for bounds check, allowing out-of-bounds array access when index equals nphys (array size). This off-by-one error leads to reading/writing beyond the allocated phy array.
